newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union sues to retain east German wage pacts.
newsitem.headline: German union sues to retain east German wage pacts.

text.p: Germany's IG Bau building sector union said on Friday it had filed an action challenging the unprecedented decision by German employers last month to scrap wage agreements for east German construction workers.
"The union is seeking legal confirmation that the wage agreements...were not, as a result, dissolved (by the decision) but remain valid," IG Bau said in a statement.
The agreements, signed earlier this year in March and April, covered wages and training funds and were designed gradually to bring conditions in the east of the country up to those in the west.

But the Hauptverband der Deutschen Bauindustrie industry association said in August the agreements were not workable because eastern firms could not finance them and that industry there was in an "emergency situation".
The two contracts were to give east German workers a 1.85-percent pay rise on September 1 and lift their salaries to 95 percent of western levels from the current 92 percent by October.
Terminating the wage deals, the German industry association said a wage freeze was the only way to even out the competitive imbalance between east and west.
IG Bau said its legal action, which will go before the Wiesbaden industrial tribunal, would seek to establish that the termination of such agreements could not be legally recognised.
